system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: Can MVFA's few-shot inference be made inductive, scoring each image only with statistics of the K normal support images and source-validation data instead of test-set min-max normalisation, while keeping image AUROC within 1 point of the re-run transductive baseline and making each image's score invariant to the composition of the rest of the test set (prevalence 10-50%, with and without outliers)? The replacement is evaluated component by component (normalisation, then fusion weight, then image-level aggregation), with sensitivity at 95% specificity and expected calibration error reported alongside AUROC.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Binomial exceedance test: per-image p-values from support-calibrated pixel thresholds
SUMMARY: Set a pixel threshold so that a known small fraction of support-normal pixels exceed it, and score each test image by the binomial tail probability of its observed number of exceeding pixels.
HYPOTHESIS: A per-image binomial exceedance p-value with the pixel threshold at the 99th percentile of support LOO fused pixel scores achieves image AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline, controls the realised false-positive rate on normal test images within 2 points of the nominal 5% after a source-fitted overdispersion correction, and is unaffected by single spurious pixels.
RATIONALE: The log-odds parent calibrates pixel probabilities and the region-mass parent aggregates excess above a support threshold, but both still need a learned or ad hoc map from pixel evidence to an image decision. A different explanation of what an image score should measure is how surprising the amount of exceedance is under the normal model: if a threshold is set so that a fraction q of normal pixels exceed it, a normal image's exceedance count is approximately binomial (with overdispersion from spatial correlation), and an abnormal image has more exceedances than expected. The resulting tail probability is a per-image p-value defined without test-set statistics, and one spurious pixel changes it by a negligible amount, which addresses the max-pixel fragility verified in MVFA's code.
METHOD: 1) Fused pixel map m(x): support LOO z-scores per branch and level, averaged (no min-max). 2) Pixel threshold t_q = (1 - q) quantile of LOO support pixel scores, q = 0.01. 3) For a test image with n pixels (on the 17x17 patch grid, n = 289, to limit spatial correlation), count c = #{x: m(x) > t_q}. 4) Overdispersion phi fitted on source-validation normal images: Var(c) = phi n q (1 - q); use a beta-binomial with matching variance. 5) Image p-value = P(C >= c); image score = -log10 p. 6) test_few.py: implement; remove min-max; threshold p <= 0.05. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support z-score. Ordered ablation: (i) support z-score normalisation with max pooling, (ii) exceedance count, (iii) binomial vs beta-binomial p-value. Metrics: image AUROC, realised FPR at p <= 0.05, AUROC under 1-5 injected spikes, score shift under resampling. Falsified if AUROC drops more than 1 point or realised FPR exceeds 7% after the overdispersion correction.

Idea B:
TITLE: Selective per-image MVFA scoring with a conformal abstention band
SUMMARY: Give each image one of three outputs, normal, abnormal or refer to a reader, by placing an abstention band on its conformal p-value, and measure the risk-coverage trade-off that a deployable MVFA would offer.
HYPOTHESIS: With an abstention band of p in [0.05, 0.3], selective MVFA scoring reaches at least 95% sensitivity and 95% specificity on the images it does not refer, while referring at most 25% of images on held-out modalities at K >= 4, which the original transductive pipeline cannot provide because its scores have no per-image meaning.
RATIONALE: The two-guarantee idea separates false-positive control from probability calibration. By analogy with clinical triage and selective classification, a screening system does not need to decide every case: it can refer uncertain images to a radiologist. A per-image conformal p-value supports exactly this, with a guaranteed false-positive rate for 'abnormal' calls and a calibrated band for referral. Measuring risk versus coverage turns MVFA's scoring into a decision tool and quantifies its clinical usefulness, which AUC alone cannot (G11).
METHOD: 1) Per-image conformal p-value from the fused inductive score (support LOO, as in the conformal parent). 2) Decision: abnormal if p < alpha_lo, normal if p > alpha_hi, refer otherwise; alpha_lo = 0.05; alpha_hi chosen on source episodes to give 95% negative predictive value. 3) Report coverage, selective sensitivity and specificity, and the risk-coverage curve over alpha_hi in [0.05, 0.5]. 4) test_few.py: implement; remove min-max. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support z-score. Conditions: no abstention; abstention band selected on source episodes; oracle band (upper reference). Metrics: coverage, selective sensitivity/specificity, area under the risk-coverage curve, score shift under resampling. Falsified if selective sensitivity and specificity do not both reach 95% at 75% coverage at K >= 4.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
